identity.name: Tidy
identity.value_proposition: Rename messy downloaded files into a consistent, sortable form.
identity.target_users: People whose download folders fill up with files named like IMG_2041 (3).JPG.

requirements.text: A user can rename every file in a folder to a date-prefixed, lowercase, hyphenated name.
requirements.acceptance: Given a folder with files named 'IMG 2041 (3).JPG', when the user runs tidy on it, then the file is renamed to '2026-10-23-img-2041-3.jpg' and nothing else changes.

components.name: cli
components.responsibility: Renames the files in a folder by a fixed naming rule.

releases.process: Tag vX.Y.Z on main; CI builds the binaries and attaches them to the GitHub release.

decisions.title: Product identity
decisions.context: A small tool for one tidy-up job.
decisions.decision: Tidy renames files for people with messy download folders.
decisions.consequences: Features beyond R1 need a new requirement first.

decisions.title: One Rust CLI
decisions.context: A single command-line tool, distributed as a binary.
decisions.decision: One Rust component at the repository root.
decisions.consequences: Rust's toolchain is the only one to maintain; its recipe is drafted for this project.

decisions.title: One binary, no contracts
decisions.context: Nothing calls the CLI but people.
decisions.decision: cli renames files by a fixed rule.

decisions.title: Messages and exit codes
decisions.context: People run it in a terminal.
decisions.decision: Errors go to stderr with a fix and a non-zero exit code.
decisions.consequences: Scripts can rely on the exit code.

decisions.title: Unit and end-to-end tests
decisions.context: The rename rule is the core; the folder walk is the risk.
decisions.decision: cli: unit tests for the rule, end-to-end tests on a temp folder.
decisions.consequences: Tests name the requirement they cover.

decisions.title: No UI
decisions.context: The project has no user interface.
decisions.decision: There is no visual system to define.

decisions.title: README is the user documentation
decisions.decision: User docs live in the README.
decisions.consequences: Map paths once the CLI has a public interface.

decisions.title: GitHub Actions, a binary, not deployed
decisions.decision: CI runs the checks; the artifact is a binary.

decisions.title: No secrets, no auth
decisions.decision: Nothing is deployed and nobody signs in.
decisions.consequences: Revisit if it ever talks to a service.

decisions.title: Monthly Dependabot updates
decisions.decision: Dependabot opens monthly updates for crates and CI actions.

decisions.title: Semver with GitHub releases
decisions.decision: Semver tags on main; release notes live in GitHub releases.
decisions.consequences: A breaking flag change bumps the major version.

decisions.title: No stored data
decisions.context: The CLI keeps no data of its own.

decisions.title: No accessibility target
decisions.context: The project has no user interface.

decisions.title: Startup under 200 ms
decisions.context: The CLI runs in shell loops.
decisions.decision: Startup stays under 200 ms, measured with hyperfine in CI.
decisions.consequences: A slower startup needs a decision record.

decisions.title: Conventional commits on trunk
decisions.context: A solo maintainer with agents committing.
decisions.decision: Conventional commits scoped by component, on trunk.
decisions.consequences: The commit-msg hook rejects other messages.

decisions.title: Batched review
decisions.decision: Batched review at 200 lines or 5 files.
decisions.consequences: Agents stop for review past either limit.
